summary: The QuickEntryFindStudent file facilitates the searching and selection of students for various operations, such as placements, based on parameters including last name, first name, student number, and program consent. It includes features like selection of all or none, validation, and client-side scripting for enhanced interaction.
purpose: To enable quick searching and handling of student records based on various attributes, allowing for efficient student placement and enrollment workflows.

fields.name: lastName
fields.description: Last name of the student for search filtering.

fields.name: firstName
fields.description: First name of the student for search filtering.

fields.name: studentNumber
fields.description: Unique identifier for a student used in search filtering.

fields.name: ProgramID
fields.description: ID of the program related to the consent.

fields.name: includeNoConsent
fields.description: Flag to include students with no consent in the search results.

actors.name: User
actors.role: Interacts with the system to search and select students.

workflows.name: Student Search and Selection
steps: User enters search criteria such as last name, first name, or student number.
User selects a program for filtering consent-related entries.
Client-side validation ensures at least one search criterion is filled.
Search results are displayed in a grid, with options to select students.
User can select all or none of the search results using available buttons.
Selected student IDs are processed for further operations.

business_rules: Student searches require at least one non-empty search field.
validations: Fields for search criteria cannot be all empty.
conditions: Display a program warning if the selected program does not match the current filter.
system_behavior: Registers client-side scripts to manage search interactions and validation.
Uses server controls to bind search results to a grid for user interaction.
dependencies: ASP.NET framework and controls for UI management.
exceptions: JavaScript validation failures result in client-side messages prompting user action.
